comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the liveness probe is blind to `queued` runs — the "pool appears IDLE" warning false-fires on the exact healthy-queue shape gh-1903 is about**

The probe lists only `--status in_progress` (also `--limit 20`). GitHub run statuses are `queued` / `in_progress` / `completed`, so a sibling leg's freshly-dispatched child that is itself still **queued** for fa-m5-1 is invisible to this probe. In the 2026-10-26 incident shape — the testflight child queued while the cli sibling chain holds/waits on the pool — the early window (siblings dispatched but not yet picked up) makes the probe return **zero** rows, and the script then logs:

```
::warning:: repo-wide in_progress runs: NONE ... pool appears IDLE (gh-172 zombie signature possible ...)
```

on a perfectly healthy queue. The header comment's claim — "Only a repo-wide EMPTY in_progress list while the child never started positively establishes pool idleness" (script line 33) — is therefore false: queued runs are invisible to it. Two smaller distortions ride along:

- `--limit 20` truncates: a repo with >20 busy runs can read "0" here while the pool is saturated.
- The opposite direction: any `in_progress` run on a *hosted* runner (ci on ubuntu-latest, unrelated to fa-m5-1) is logged as "the queued child is waiting behind these" — which may not be true either.

Nothing cancels (gh-1903 holds — this is diagnostic-only), but a `::warning::` crying "zombie signature possible" during the exact healthy scenario this PR exists to protect will train readers to ignore the real warning. Options: (a) also probe `--status queued` (or run the listing unfiltered and bucket by status) before ever claiming idleness; (b) or downgrade the message to "no in_progress runs observed — queued runs are invisible to this probe; idleness cannot be established" and reserve the zombie-signature wording for the trap diagnostic.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the orphan-cancel decides from possibly-stale state — an API outage (or a start between the last poll and the TERM) can cancel a child that actually STARTED**

The trap gates the cancel on `child_started` and `last_state` — both records of the *last successful observation*, which may be minutes old at signal time:

- If polls have been failing (sustained gh/API outage), `child_started` stays 0 and `last_state` is `error/-` even though the child may be mid-build. The trap then cancels a **running** child — exactly what the PR's own invariant forbids ("A child that ever started — even if it is between jobs right now — is left alone").
- Even without an outage, a child picked up by the pool between the final poll and the runner's SIGTERM is cancelled while starting.

This is the one place "cannot observe ⇒ cannot judge" is violated: every other cancel path was deleted for this principle, yet the surviving path judges from a cache. The trap is not latency-sensitive (the leg is already dead, and `gh run cancel` is one call), so a single fresh re-check before cancelling both honors the invariant and shrinks the diagnostic:

```bash
fresh="$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,jobs \
  --jq '"\(.status) " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued")] | length | tostring)' 2>/dev/null)" || fresh=""
# cancel only when fresh proves never-started (status in_progress/queued with
# zero started jobs — or keep the cancel on empty fresh, but say why)
```

At minimum, when `last_state` is `error/-` the diagnostic should say the cancel decision was made on stale/unobservable state rather than presenting `NEVER STARTED` as fact.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the stub's `is_jobs` detection block is duplicated — hoist it**

The `--json ... jobs` argument scan appears twice inside the `view)` handler (the block at line 165 gates `jobs_body` construction; the block at line 195 re-detects the same flag to choose the output format and append to `jobs-served-<id>.log`). Both scan identical args and can never disagree, so the second copy is pure duplication in a fixture whose comments elsewhere go to great lengths to stay precise. Compute `is_jobs` once at the top of the `view)` handler and reuse it in both places.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: The watchdog removal is sound and well-tested — all 25 tests in `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` pass locally, shellcheck is clean, `--budget-seconds`/`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` are gone from workflows and script, legs retain `actions: write` so the one surviving cancel path is permitted, and the gh-1903 invariants (read-only wait, exactly-one orphan-cancel on TERM/INT, no re-dispatch) are each pinned by a dedicated test.

**Key Issues** (none blocking):
1. ⚠️ The repo-wide liveness probe lists only `--status in_progress` — `queued` sibling runs are invisible, so the "pool appears IDLE (gh-172 zombie signature)" `::warning::` false-fires during the exact healthy-queue scenario gh-1903 protects (details in the inline comment).
2. ⚠️ The orphan-cancel trap decides from last-observed state; an API outage (or a pickup between last poll and TERM) can make it cancel a child that actually started — one fresh `gh run view` re-check in the trap would close this (inline comment).
3. 💡 `watch_started=0` until the watch loop makes the trap's elapsed diagnostic print ~1.7 billion seconds if TERM lands in the appear window.
4. 💡 The stub `gh`'s `is_jobs` scan is duplicated in the `view)` handler — hoist it.

**Next Steps**:
1. Probe `--status queued` too (or stop claiming positive idleness) before emitting the zombie-signature warning.
2. Re-check the child's live state inside the orphan-cancel trap before cancelling.
3. Init `watch_started` at script start; hoist the stub's duplicate `is_jobs` detection.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
📍 **`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh:138`**

💡 **SUGGESTION: `watch_started=0` makes the trap's elapsed arithmetic explode if TERM lands during dispatch/appear**

`watch_started` is only set when the watch loop begins (line 169). If the leg is cancelled (or its timeout fires) while the script is still in `dispatch`/`wait_for_run` — a 10-minute appear window inside a 150–360m leg, and manual cancels happen — the trap prints `leg terminated by TERM after $((now - 0))s`, i.e. ~1.7 billion seconds, in the very diagnostic this PR touts. Initialize once at script start (e.g. `watch_started=$(date +%s)` before `dispatch`) so "after Ns" means leg-elapsed from the runner's perspective in every path.
